summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.5% YoY to Rs 9,008 million, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 18.5% and FY27 revenue guided up 50%.
summary.overview: Fujiyama reported a strong March quarter, with revenue of Rs 9,008 million (+87.5% YoY, +53.1% QoQ) and PAT of Rs 1,063 million (11.8% margin). Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 26,545 million (+72.3%) and PAT Rs 3,041 million (11.5% margin). Capacity expansion continued at Ratlam, with the 2 GW solar panel plant commissioned, though the inverter and battery lines slipped to 2027. A fire at the Bawal lead-acid battery facility (1.3 GW capacity) has suspended operations, with third-party arrangements covering supply. Management guided FY27 revenue up 50% and PAT margin of 11% to 13%.

segments.name: Solar panels
segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 1,039 MW to 1,639 MW during FY26. Management estimated Q4 revenue mix at roughly 40% panels, 40% power electronics and 20% batteries, which it said fluctuates.

segments.name: Power electronics (inverters)
segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 1,143 MW to 2,180 MW during FY26. Inverter line at Ratlam is expected to be commissioned in Q1 2027.

segments.name: Lithium-ion batteries
segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 45 MWh to 545 MWh during FY26. Battery machinery orders are placed, with commissioning expected in Q2 2027.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries (Bawal)
segments.commentary: Facility with 1.3 GW capacity suspended after a fire; no casualties. Management said it is covered by insurance and third-party capacity is being used.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 50%.
FY27 PAT margin guided at 11% to 13%; management said margins are stable to improving.
Indicative FY27 quarterly revenue split: Q1 about Rs 900 crore, Q2 about Rs 800 crore, Q3 about Rs 800 crore, Q4 about Rs 1,500 crore.
Ratlam 2 GW integrated facility expected to reach peak revenue of about Rs 5,000 crore, fully utilised by Q4 FY28; utilisation about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28.
Management said no promoter stake sale or fundraise is planned for the next 12 months.
capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity at Ratlam (2 GW integrated facility) commissioned; inverter line machinery received and commissioning expected Q1 2027; battery lines Q2 2027.
Planned 1,200 MW TOPCon solar cell line at Ratlam, capex about Rs 350 crore excluding land (land largely acquired in earlier phases); orders not yet placed as of the call.
Existing Mono PERC cell capacity is 1,000 MW; no plan to upgrade it to TOPCon for now.

Existing line commissioned in FY26 running at about 65% utilisation at exit, expected to reach about 80% in a month or two; overall FY26 utilisation was 70% to 80% across products, with lithium batteries still catching up.
demand_pricing: Channel network crossed 8,900 partners by March 2026, after adding 80+ distributors, 450+ dealers and 30 exclusive outlets in Q4.
FY26 sales were about 1 GW of integrated SPGS systems; management said growth was volume-led, roughly 70% in GW terms.
Demand driven by off-grid and hybrid backup in Tier 2/3 towns and villages; management said Tier 1 on-grid sales were now being added.
Management said over 7 million PM Surya Ghar installations remain untapped, about 25 GW opportunity; ALMM List-II is expected soon and will require DCR cells.
Management said it is passing margin to customers to acquire distributors and dealers, and that competition is mainly in ground-mounted business.
Receivables are from distributors only; revenue cycle about 14 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply, and what is the raw material vs finished goods split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is mainly raw material for new locations (Dadri, Noida, Ratlam); raw material is above Rs 500 crore of about Rs 900 crore total inventory, and finished goods inventory days are similar to last year. Management expects inventory days to fall once lines ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Bawal fire: is the facility operational and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations are suspended and the cause is under investigation. Management said margin impact is slight, offset by third-party lead-acid capacity bought at good prices, and that the incident will not have a material long-term impact.

qa_highlights.question: BIS seizures: what was affected and what is the penalty exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10 to 15 of about 500 SKUs, mainly inverters and batteries, are under BIS query. The maximum penalty equals the seizure value, but management expects a lower outcome. It said there is no impact on the Dadri or Ratlam ramp-up or PM Surya Ghar participation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and margin contributions from the Ratlam and TOPCon cell lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Ratlam peak revenue is about Rs 5,000 crore when fully utilised. The TOPCon cell line adds no revenue, only backward integration and margin benefit. Management said it is passing DCR margin to customers rather than retaining it.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term PAT margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 PAT margin at 11% to 13%, said margins are stable to improving, and cited AI-led opex reduction. It did not give a 36-month target.

risks_watch: Bawal fire: cause unknown, operations suspended, and reliance on third-party lead-acid supply.
BIS query on 10 to 15 SKUs (inverters and batteries), with a court decision pending.
Inventory days rose from about 120 to about 180; raw material build needs to unwind as Ratlam ramps up.
Ratlam ramp-up is slipping: inverter and battery lines are delayed to 2027 and utilisation is 50% in FY27.
Competitive intensity as new capacity comes online; management said it may trade margin for distributor growth.
Management declined to disclose segment-wise or megawatt volumes, which limits verification of the 50% guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 growth guide, but cautious on timelines (inverter and battery lines slipped to 2027) and evasive on segment volumes and market share, citing competition.
key_quotes: We are relieved to share that there were no casualties or injuries, and the safety and wellness of our employees and workers remain our highest priority.
Backward integration improves the margins, not the revenue, sir.
Sir, for coming year, you can consider the guidance 11% to 13% basically for PAT margin.
